# Decisions we made

The Oct 28 meeting settled the project's experimental design. The relevant decisions were:

| # | Decision | Options | Our lean |
|---|----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Dataset | `derek-thomas/ScienceQA` (all) vs `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG` (image-only) | Image-only for main experiments |
| 2 | Softmax variant | One forward pass reading $P(A/B/C/D)$ vs $k=8$ sampling only | Both; softmax as additional variant |
| 3 | Baselines | Oracle (ground-truth labels) + $\tau=0$ (no filtering) | Both, adopted from Shiqi's suggestion |
| 4 | VQAv2 scope | Main / stretch / drop | Stretch (ScienceQA first) |

The dataset decision was the only genuinely open item. `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG` was image-only by construction (every row had an image, zero text-only), whereas `derek-thomas/ScienceQA` added the text-only half. Since the project was about a **V**LM, image-only became the main experiment and text-only a secondary analysis. The two datasets were row-for-row aligned on the image+text half, so switching between them was lossless for the vision experiments.

# Progress since the meeting

All six action items from the meeting were completed.

| # | Action item | Owner | Status |
|-|----|-|------|
| 1 | Confirmed SCF GPU allocation | Matt | Done --- one NVIDIA TITAN Xp (12 GB), driver 570.124.06, CUDA 12.8. Partition `gpu` had `PreemptMode=REQUEUE`, so jobs were checkpointed. |
| 2 | Set up Python env on SCF; confirmed SmolVLM loads | Matt | Done --- conda env `smolvlm` (Python 3.11), torch 2.14.1+cu126, transformers 5.x. SmolVLM-500M loaded at `cuda:0`, `torch.bfloat16`, 507.48M params. |
| 3 | HF Hub repo for checkpoints | Matt | Done --- `mattbix/cs289-smolvlm-checkpoints`, with both baseline JSONLs under `baselines/`. |
| 4 | `scripts/01_baseline_eval.py` --- zero-shot greedy on 500-question subset | Matt | Done --- results are reported below. |
| 5 | ScienceQA counts, image+text vs. text-only, per split | Matt, Shiqi | Done --- counts are reported below; Matt ran the counts, Shiqi reviewed. |
| 6 | SmolVLM forward-pass API notes for softmax over options | Matt, Shiqi | Done --- `scripts/02_softmax_eval.py`; Matt implemented and ran it, Shiqi reviewed. |

Two notes on the infrastructure. First, the `gpu` partition's single TITAN Xp was small but sufficient: SmolVLM-500M occupied about 1.1 GB at bf16 inference, so LoRA fine-tuning fit comfortably. The real constraint was `PreemptMode=REQUEUE` --- long runs were checkpointed per example, which the baseline scripts did (JSONL append after every question). Second, the HF Hub token was stored under `$HOME` (`~/.cache/huggingface/token`), so it survived login-node changes; `HF_HOME` was exported from both `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` to cover interactive `srun` and `sbatch` contexts alike.

# Preliminary results

## Dataset counts

| Dataset | Split | Total | Image+text | Text-only |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG` | train | 6,218 | 6,218 | 0 |
| | validation | 2,097 | 2,097 | 0 |
| | test | 2,017 | 2,017 | 0 |
| `derek-thomas/ScienceQA` | train | 12,726 | 6,218 | 6,508 |
| | validation | 4,241 | 2,097 | 2,144 |
| | test | 4,241 | 2,017 | 2,224 |

The image+text column of `derek-thomas/ScienceQA` matched `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG` row-for-row, confirming the two datasets were aligned. The main experiments therefore used `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG`; the text-only rows were held out for a secondary analysis.

## Baselines (500-question image-only test subset, seed 0)

Both baselines were evaluated on the same 500-question random subset of `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG` test, so row-by-row comparison was valid.

| Variant | Accuracy | Forward passes per question |
|---|--:|----|
| Zero-shot greedy | 0.6480 (324/500) | 1 autoregressive decode, $\leq 8$ tokens |
| Zero-shot softmax argmax | **0.6700** (335/500) | 1 single pass, no decode |

The softmax variant was both cheaper (one forward pass versus an autoregressive decode) and slightly more accurate (+2.2 points, 11 more correct). That was the headline result of the ablation: the graded-confidence signal captured information the sampled-mode signal did not.

## Ablation split (greedy vs. softmax, same 500)

| Outcome | Count |
|---|---:|
| Agreed on predicted letter | 373 / 500 (74.6%) |
| Both right | 276 |
| Greedy-only right | 48 |
| Softmax-only right | 59 |

Check: $276 + 48 = 324$ (greedy total), $276 + 59 = 335$ (softmax total).

The two methods disagreed on a quarter of the questions (127/500), and on those disagreements softmax was right slightly more often (59 vs 48). Neither method dominated. This supported running both as an ablation rather than choosing one: the sampling-based consistency signal and the softmax-confidence signal were complementary, not redundant. The 107 questions on which exactly one method was correct were the recoverable headroom for the consistency-filter fine-tuning stage.

# Remaining work

The meeting's action items were closed before the progress report was due. The remaining research milestones would proceed as follows.

1. **Consistency-filter fine-tuning.** The filter at threshold $\tau$ would be implemented, and the two comparison baselines (oracle on ground-truth labels; $\tau=0$, no filtering) agreed at the meeting would be run. This was the experiment that would isolate the contribution of the filter.
2. **SmolVLM pseudo-label generation.** The $k=8$ sampled outputs on the training split would be generated, with mode and frequency extracted, and the high-consensus subset selected.
3. **LoRA fine-tuning.** LoRA on SmolVLM-500M at bf16 would be run; the TITAN Xp's 12 GB would be sufficient.
4. **Post-fine-tuning evaluation.** Both baselines would be re-run on the fine-tuned model and compared against the 0.6480 / 0.6700 figures above.
5. **Write-up.** The two baseline tables and the ablation split above would become the paper's first results section; the consistency-filter comparison would become the second.
